nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic activities... were evaluated by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) in 0.5 M H2SO4 at a scan rate of 5 mV s^{-1} in a three-electrode system... All potentials were iR corrected and referenced to the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE)... The YCR catalyst exhibits an overpotential of 275 mV at 10 mA cm^{-2}... Tafel slope of YCR (61 mV dec^{-1})... The C_dl value of... YCR (6.3 mF cm^{-2})... EIS... revealed a better charge transfer of YCR... after 2000 cycles, the overpotential... decreased by 3.6% for YCR.

The YCR catalyst exhibits an overpotential of 275 mV at 10 mA cm^{-2}, which is smaller than parent YR (360 mV)... The Tafel slope of YCR (61 mV dec^{-1}) is smaller compared to YR (118 mV dec^{-1})... The C_dl value of... YR (6.6 mF cm^{-2})... after 2000 cycles, the overpotential... 8.6% for YR.

The YCR catalyst exhibits an overpotential of 275 mV at 10 mA cm^{-2}, which is smaller than... commercial RuO_2 (286 mV). The Tafel slope of YCR... compares favorably to that of RuO_2 (86 mV dec^{-1})... The C_dl value of RuO_2 is 16.8 mF cm^{-2}... after 2000 cycles... 9.9% for RuO_2.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 0.5 M H2SO4
nodes.source_text: Meanwhile, the YCR also displays better compared to commercial RuO_2 for water splitting in a two-electrode configuration in 0.5 M H2SO4 at 25°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: YR and YCR powders calcined at 1100°C match cubic Y₂Ru₂O₇ phase (space group Fb-3m #227) with small high angle shift due to Co substitution and no impurities detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The room temperature powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns of the YR and YCR powders calcined at 1100°C are displayed in Figure 1a.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows Y, Ru, O, Co coexistence; HRXPS confirms unchanged Y 3d, Co 2p peaks at 780.50 eV (2p3/2) and 795.98 eV (2p1/2) with increasing separation indicating Co reduction, Ru 3p high energy shift from Ru4+ to Ru5+, O 1s shows higher surface oxygen species in YCR (63 at.%) vs YR (54 at%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was applied to explore the possible variation in the oxidation state of yttrium, ruthenium, and oxygen with changes in cobalt concentrations.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows increased particle size of YCR compared to YR attributed to Co incorporation; particle diameter increases from 155 nm (YR) to 400 nm (Co-30).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of YR and YCR powders was investigated via a scanning electron microscope (SEM) (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDS mapping proves uniform distribution of Y, Ru, O, and Co in YCR with no chemical segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The uniform distribution of Y, Ru, O, and Co in YCR was proven by SEM-EDS mapping (Figure S8, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals YR morphology with [112] zone axis, d-spacing 0.59 nm (111) plane and 0.356 nm between Y/Ru columns; YCR shows [001] zone axis, d-spacing 0.252 nm (200) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To understand the structure of the material, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms YR (110) and (440) Bragg diffraction along [112] zone axis; YCR shows (220) diffraction spots along [001] zone axis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d shows the morphology of YR particles. The red circle in Figure 1d represents the area used for selected area electron-diffraction (SAED) (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows atomic model occupancy for YR [112] projection (Y green dots, Ru white dots) and YCR [001] projection with d-spacings matching crystal planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image of the same area with [112] projection view is shown in Figure 1f.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS mapping shows no chemical segregation in YR and YCR particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g shows the element distribution in the YR particles. No chemical segregation was observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows peak at g=2.002 due to oxygen vacancies; YCR peak intensity 16 times higher than YR.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2f and Figure S17 (Supporting Information) show peaks (EPR signal) with a g factor = 2.002, due to single electrons trapped in oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: YCR electrical conductivity 36.8 Ω⁻¹m⁻¹ vs YR 5.6 Ω⁻¹m⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electronic conductivity of YCR (36.8Ω⁻¹m⁻¹) is much higher than that of YR (5.6Ω⁻¹m⁻¹), as shown in Figure 2i.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows positive shift for YR/YCR vs RuO₂ indicating Ru oxidation; YCR more positive than YR confirming further Ru oxidation; EXAFS shows Ru-O at 1.51-1.52 Å, Ru-Ru(Co) shift 2.58 to 2.51 Å, CN reduced from 6.1 to 5.4 (first shell), 2.0 to 0.7 (second shell).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electronic state and local coordination environment of Ru and Co were further investigated in detail via X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) measurements on YR and YCR.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES higher energy than CoO indicating Co oxidation state slightly >+2; EXAFS shows Co-O at 1.51 Å and Co-Ru at 2.76 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge XANES spectra of YCR were located at a higher energy value position compared to CoO, which indicates the oxidation state of Co in YCR just a little higher than +2 (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values: RuO₂ 16.8 mF cm⁻², YR 6.6 mF cm⁻², YCR 6.3 mF cm⁻² indicating no significant ECSA increase for YCR vs YR.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical double-layer capacitance Cdl (Figure S25, Supporting Information) was determined from the cyclic voltammetry (CV) data.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows better charge transfer for YCR compared to YR and RuO₂ at 1.5 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was conducted as shown in Figure 4f, which also revealed a better charge transfer of YCR compared to YR and RuO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT PDOS shows reduced bandgap from 0.96 eV (YR) to 0.63 eV (YCR); differential charge density confirms electronic structure changes; YCR predicted higher conductivity confirmed experimentally.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To investigate the effect of cobalt atoms in the Y2-xCoxRu2O7 system on the electronic structure, the partial density of state (PDOS) of YR and YCR catalysts were calculated using density functional theory (DFT) as shown in Figure 2g.
